clue.text: Many a declaration is made with the second on the first and the first in the second

definitions.text: Many a declaration is made with the second on the first and the first in the second

parts.words: Many a declaration is made with the second on the first and the first in the second
parts.note: the answer's words are numbered: the second (a palm) laid on the first (the organ of love), and that organ given into the palm, as in a vow of devotion

explanation.surface: A puzzling riddle about how solemn declarations are made, using numbered parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The second on the first' is a hand placed on the heart; 'the first in the second' is the heart offered in the hand. Both are gestures of a lover's pledge.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes complete devotion, the kind promised in a proposal of marriage.

clue.text: Sums are rising

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters are read from the bottom upward, so backwards

explanation.surface: Arithmetic totals going up, as in a growing bill.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is left implicit: the reversed letters spell the name of the Dutch Renaissance scholar, so the whole clue is the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The great Dutch humanist scholar of the Renaissance, author of In Praise of Folly.

clue.text: He stands on ceremony

parts.note: to stand on ceremony is to insist on formality; read literally, a man whose position is built on rites

explanation.definitionFit: Someone devoted to rites and formal observances literally takes ceremony as their ground.

clue.text: Assign

parts.note: a plain one-word definition: to apportion or set aside for a purpose

explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to apportion or earmark something for a person or purpose.

clue.text: Just the thing for a nightworker

definitions.text: Just the thing for a nightworker

parts.words: Just the thing for a nightworker
parts.note: someone who works through the night must sleep in daylight, so a couch for daytime rest suits them literally

explanation.definitionFit: A couch for resting on in daytime, literally the sleeping place of someone who works nights.

clue.text: " Carries as the flint bears fire" (J. Caesar)

definitions.text: " Carries as the flint bears fire" (J. Caesar)

parts.words: " Carries as the flint bears fire" (J. Caesar)
parts.note: a missing-word quotation: Brutus says he is yoked with a lamb 'that carries ... as the flint bears fire', hiding a hot temper that sparks briefly

explanation.walkthrough: Fill the gap in Shakespeare's Julius Caesar, Act 4 Scene 3, where Brutus describes his own brief flashes of temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Rage, the passion struck out briefly like a spark from flint, is the word Shakespeare uses.

clue.text: Not the sort fitted to an eight-day clock

definitions.text: Not the sort fitted to an eight-day clock

parts.words: Not the sort fitted to an eight-day clock
parts.note: an eight-day clock has a coiled spring that runs for eight days; one lasting a single day would be the opposite, but the word really means dawn

explanation.definitionFit: A poetic word for dawn, the springing up of the day, read here as a clock coil wound for one day.

clue.text: When sailors take to science one gets a taxi in a ship

definitions.text: one gets a taxi in a ship

indicators.note: the sailors attach themselves to the science, so their letters follow it

parts.note: SC is an abbreviation for science, as in BSc
ABS are able seamen, ordinary sailors

explanation.surface: A curious scene of sailors studying science and a cab carried aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: Both halves are wordplay with no true definition: the second half also builds the answer, as CAB (taxi) inside SS (steamship). The word means crusts over healing wounds, or strike-breakers.
explanation.definitionFit: Here a second wordplay stands in for the definition: a cab placed inside the steamship abbreviation SS.

clue.text: Always in hindrance, this quadruped

indicators.note: the word for always is put inside the word for hindrance

parts.note: a let is an old word for an obstacle, as in 'without let or hindrance'
ever means always

explanation.surface: An animal that is forever getting in the way.
explanation.definitionFit: A young hare in its first year, a four-legged animal.

clue.text: Culinary example of bad singing

parts.note: a chant is a kind of singing
illy is an old adverb meaning badly, so chanting done illy is bad singing

explanation.surface: Tuneless warbling in the kitchen, offered as a cooking specimen.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads 'bad singing' but the answer puts the singing first and the badly after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweetened whipped cream named after a French town is a classic item of cookery.

clue.text: Wilkie Collins's Sir Percival

parts.note: the scheming baronet in the Victorian novel The Woman in White has this surname

explanation.definitionFit: Sir Percival is the villainous husband in The Woman in White, a Victorian mystery novel.

clue.text: Explosive aspect of Ferdinand II

parts.note: the King of the Two Sicilies earned a nickname by shelling his own rebel cities in 1848

explanation.definitionFit: King Ferdinand II of the Two Sicilies was nicknamed after his bombardment of Messina and Palermo.

clue.text: What a sweet flower !

parts.note: read as exclaiming over a lovely bloom, but 'sweet' is a dessert: the name is both a fruit tart and a cottage-garden plant

explanation.definitionFit: The name is both a fruit dessert and a popular nickname for heliotrope, a fragrant garden plant.

clue.text: Helps

parts.note: a plain one-word definition: gives aid or support

explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: lends aid or support to someone.

clue.text: It's a bit rough on the hands

definitions.text: It's a bit rough on the hands

parts.words: It's a bit rough on the hands
parts.note: sounds like a complaint about harsh treatment, but describes a lump of abrasive volcanic stone used to scrub skin

explanation.definitionFit: A light porous volcanic stone used to rub hard skin smooth, literally a rough piece applied to hands.

clue.text: Tumult am I? Certainly the making of it

definitions.text: Tumult am I? Certainly the making of it

indicators.note: the letters of the first words are what the answer is made from, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A final demand asks whether it is uproar, and admits it is the cause of one.
explanation.definitionFit: A final demand with a threat attached, which is certainly the making of a tumult.

clue.text: Timothy on a package making a pie'

indicators.note: in a down clue the name sits on top of the package

parts.note: Tim is the short form of the name Timothy
a bale is a large bound package of goods

explanation.surface: A man called Timothy sits on a parcel and somehow produces a pie.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish of meat or fish cooked in a pastry case or drum-shaped mould.

clue.text: In the nature of things, it's only productive if well oiled

definitions.text: In the nature of things, it's only productive if well oiled

parts.words: In the nature of things, it's only productive if well oiled
parts.note: 'well oiled' suggests a smooth-running machine or a drunk, but literally a conduit from an oil well is useful only when the well yields

explanation.definitionFit: A long conduit carrying oil from a well, useful only when the well is producing.

clue.text: I put 'em right

indicators.note: putting the letters right means setting them in a new, correct order

explanation.surface: Someone confidently claims to set things straight.
explanation.definitionFit: To attribute or lay blame on someone, that is, to put a fault on them.

clue.text: Vegetable is fish

parts.note: a pea is a vegetable
is shortens to 's, as in 'it's'
cod is a fish

explanation.surface: A baffling claim that a vegetable is really a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic name for the pod of the pea plant, itself a vegetable.

clue.text: "O, for a draught of that had been Cooled a long age in the deep-delved earth" (Keats)

definitions.text: "O, for a draught of that had been Cooled a long age in the deep-delved earth" (Keats)

parts.words: "O, for a draught of that had been Cooled a long age in the deep-delved earth" (Keats)
parts.note: a missing-word quotation from Ode to a Nightingale: the poet longs for a drink of old, cellar-cooled wine

explanation.walkthrough: Fill the gap in the second stanza of Keats's Ode to a Nightingale.
explanation.definitionFit: Wine of a good year, aged long in a cellar, is the word Keats uses.

clue.text: No doubt the poet was just a nipper once

definitions.text: No doubt the poet was just a nipper once

parts.words: No doubt the poet was just a nipper once
parts.note: a nipper is a small child, but also a creature with pincers; the poet's surname is that shellfish with one extra letter

explanation.definitionFit: George Crabbe was an English poet, author of The Borough; his name suggests a pincered shellfish.

clue.text: A guess isn't quite enough for employment

indicators.note: a loose old-style signal that the remaining letters are rearranged to stand for the answer
falling short by a little means one letter is dropped from the words

explanation.surface: A rough estimate falls short when it comes to a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'isn't quite enough' takes one S from A GUESS, leaving AGUES, which is then rearranged; the anagram is barely signalled, as often in early Times puzzles.
explanation.definitionFit: Use or employment of something, as in the usage of a tool or a word.

clue.text: This place should show whether intelligence is hereditary

definitions.text: This place should show whether intelligence is hereditary

parts.words: This place should show whether intelligence is hereditary
parts.note: a family tree of minds would chart inherited cleverness; the place name splits into a word for intelligence and a word for a pedigree chart

explanation.definitionFit: An Essex market town, whose name splits into words for intellect and a family pedigree.

clue.text: " Thy liquid that close the Eye of day " (Milton)

definitions.text: " Thy liquid that close the Eye of day " (Milton)

parts.words: " Thy liquid that close the Eye of day " (Milton)
parts.note: a missing-word quotation from Milton's sonnet To the Nightingale, about the bird's evening song

explanation.walkthrough: Fill the gap in Milton's sonnet To the Nightingale, addressed to the bird singing at dusk.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical sounds of birdsong, the liquid tones that end the day.

clue.text: The tea-time delicacies don't get in but the hands do

indicators.note: the letters of the word in are left out of the word for the delicacies

parts.note: muffins are a traditional British tea-time treat

explanation.surface: Tea-time cakes are kept away, but hands reach for them anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'the hands do (get in)': hands go into fur tubes worn for warmth.
explanation.definitionFit: Tubes of fur or cloth into which hands are slipped to keep warm.

clue.text: Forge

parts.note: a plain one-word definition in the sense of to fake or counterfeit

explanation.definitionFit: To forge can mean to fake or invent falsely, as a pretence is faked.

clue.text: It shows what a cleat is made of

definitions.text: It shows what a cleat is made of

indicators.note: what something is made of are its components, so the word cleat's letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A description of the material of a nautical fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: A kind of braid or tape lace, which shows the letters a cleat is made of.

clue.text: The fish don't necessarily need a shave

definitions.meaning: a variant spelling of a small Norwegian sprat-like fish
having stiff hairs standing up, so not necessarily needing a razor

explanation.surface: Bewhiskered fish that, despite appearances, need no razor.
explanation.definitionFit: Variant name of the sprat-like fish, and an adjective for being covered in stiff upright hairs.

clue.text: How untidy the devil's men are!

definitions.text: How untidy the devil's men are!

indicators.note: untidy letters are disordered, so the words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An exclamation at the scruffiness of Satan's followers.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of untidiness or rumpled disorder, which describes the scruffy devil's men.
